implementation_notes: Server-side Swift default: the model is a final class conforming to Model whose properties are annotated with property wrappers (@ID(key: .id), @Field(key: "email_address"), @Parent/@Children) and whose schema name sits in a static property; Fluent reads that wrapper metadata to build and run queries, so the class carries metadata and no SQL. Swift value types can serve as the real domain entities, with Fluent models kept at the persistence boundary when total ignorance is required.
pitfalls: Property wrappers require a reference-type model with an empty init(); structs cannot be Fluent models, so dumb structs need an explicit conversion layer.
Reading wrappedValue outside a database context can expose default/stale state - use the projected value for query building.

variants.name: SwiftData @Model macro
variants.implementation_notes: Apple-platform variant (iOS 17+/macOS 14+): annotating a class with @Model makes it a PersistentModel through a compile-time macro that generates the storage metadata; the class keeps ordinary properties and initialisers and the ModelContext remains the persistence facade, so no persistence calls appear in the model. Choose it for app code; keep separate domain types when the model must stay framework-free.
pitfalls: The macro rewrites stored properties: custom accessors or property observers on persisted attributes interact badly with the generated storage.
The model class is still the domain type, so app code couples to SwiftData - only a separate domain struct keeps full ignorance.
Schema changes need a SchemaMigrationPlan; the macro hides the schema but does not version it.
